issues.description: Method 'singFarmSong' in Farm.java has conflicting return types across artifacts. The problem statement (UML and textual task) and the template declare/expect singFarmSong() to be void and to print the song (UML: singFarmSong():void; task text: "prints the Old MacDonald had a Farm song"). The solution implements singFarmSong() as 'public String singFarmSong()' and returns the full song text. This mismatch leaves students uncertain whether to implement printing (void) or returning a String and can cause confusion when tests or templates assume the other contract.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single contract and make all artifacts consistent. Option A (preferred to match the current template and problem text): change the solution method signature to 'public void singFarmSong()' and modify the implementation to print the song lines (using System.out.println) so it matches the UML and task description. Update any tests that expected a String. Option B: if returning the full song text is desired, update the template method signature to 'public String singFarmSong()', update the problem statement to say the method returns the song text (instead of printing), and adjust the template placeholder and tests accordingly. Ensure template, problem statement, solution, and tests all use the same signature and behavior.
